name: Mutton Keema
cuisine: North India / pan-Indian (served across Mumbai Irani cafés, Muslim restaurants and homes)

ingredients.name: Mutton (goat) mince (keema)
ingredients.householdMeasure: a heaped ¾ cup, loosely packed

equipment: Kadai or heavy-bottomed pan (about 20 cm) with a lid
Wooden spoon or spatula; the back of the spoon to break mince lumps
Measuring spoons and a small kitchen scale (spoon and cup measures are given for the scale-less)

steps.title: Measure the mince
steps.text: Put 150 g mutton mince in a bowl and pat it dry with paper.
steps.tip: Keep it in the fridge until step 16.
steps.visualCue: Pink-red mince with white flecks of fat, no pooled liquid, no sour smell
steps.watchOut: Wet mince steams instead of browning later; if there is pink liquid in the pack, drain it and pat dry.
steps.funFact: In Indian cooking "mutton" means goat meat, not sheep (Indian Healthy Recipes).

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Finely chop ½ medium onion (70 g).
steps.visualCue: Small even pieces, about ½ cup
steps.watchOut: Big uneven chunks stay raw while the small ones burn; if so, chop the large pieces smaller before adding.

steps.title: Chop the tomato
steps.text: Chop ½ large tomato (70 g) into small pieces.
steps.watchOut: Large pieces take long to melt, leaving a thin masala; chop them small.

steps.title: Make the ginger-garlic
steps.text: Mince 1 cm ginger (5 g) and 2 garlic cloves (6 g) fine, or crush in a mortar.
steps.visualCue: A coarse wet paste with a sharp smell
steps.watchOut: Coarse pieces of garlic burn into bitter specks in the pan; mince fine.

steps.title: Chop the chilli
steps.tip: Remove the seeds for less heat.
steps.watchOut: Chilli on your fingers burns eyes later; wash your hands with soap, not water alone.

steps.title: Chop the coriander
steps.text: Chop 1 tbsp (5 g) coriander leaves; cut a ¼ lemon wedge.
steps.visualCue: Fresh green leaves, bright lemon wedge
steps.watchOut: Wet coriander turns to mush when chopped; pat it dry first.

steps.title: Mix the powders
steps.text: In a small bowl, put ¼ tsp (0.5 g) turmeric, ¾ tsp (2 g) red chilli powder and 1 tsp (3 g) coriander powder.
steps.visualCue: Three colours of powder side by side
steps.watchOut: Adding dry powders straight to hot oil scorches them (bitter smell, dark colour); keep them in the bowl until step 15.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium heat and add 12 g (1 tbsp) oil.
steps.visualCue: Oil looks thin and shimmers; a cumin seed dropped in sizzles at once
steps.watchOut: Smoking oil is too hot; lower the heat and wait 30 seconds.

steps.title: Temper the whole spices
steps.text: Add ½ tsp cumin seeds, 1 bay leaf, 1 crushed cardamom pod, 2 cloves and 3 peppercorns.
steps.visualCue: Cumin sizzles and darkens a shade within 10–15 seconds; strong sweet-spicy aroma
steps.watchOut: Black, acrid-smelling spices are burnt; if so, discard and restart with fresh oil, because the bitterness spreads.

steps.title: Brown the onion
steps.text: Add the chopped onion and cook, stirring every minute.
steps.visualCue: Soft, then translucent, then deep golden brown at the edges, with a sweet smell
steps.videoShot: Onion turning golden in the oil.
steps.watchOut: Dark brown or black edges taste bitter; lower the heat and add 1 tbsp water if it browns too fast.

steps.title: Add ginger, garlic and chilli
steps.text: Stir in the ginger-garlic and the chilli.
steps.visualCue: The raw garlic smell goes and the mixture sizzles
steps.watchOut: Garlic turning dark brown in seconds means it is burning; add a splash of water at once.

steps.title: Cook the tomato
steps.text: Add the chopped tomato and the 2.5 g salt; cook, mashing with the spoon.
steps.visualCue: Tomato breaks down to a thick paste; oil separates at the edges
steps.watchOut: A watery, pale masala with a sharp raw-tomato smell is under-cooked; keep cooking until the oil shows at the edges.

steps.title: Add the powders
steps.text: Lower the heat, add the bowl of powders and 30 ml (2 tbsp) water; stir.
steps.visualCue: Deep red-brown paste, no dry powder smell
steps.watchOut: Sticking and a burnt smell; add another splash of water and stir faster.

steps.title: Add the mince
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium-high, add the 150 g mince, break up lumps with the spoon and stir.
steps.visualCue: Colour changes from pink to grey-brown within about 3 minutes; no large lumps; the juices reduce
steps.videoShot: Mince breaking apart in the masala.
steps.watchOut: Big clumps of mince stay raw inside and make a lumpy keema; keep pressing them against the pan with the back of the spoon.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 70 ml (about 5 tbsp) water, stir and bring to a gentle boil.
steps.visualCue: Small bubbles at the edge of the pan
steps.watchOut: Too much water gives a soup; stick to 70 ml, you can add more later in small splashes.

steps.title: Simmer covered
steps.text: Lower to low heat, cover and cook, stirring twice.
steps.tip: Goat mince is tougher than chicken; if it is still chewy at 12 minutes, add 2 tbsp hot water and cook 5 minutes more.
steps.visualCue: A piece of mince crumbles easily between spoon and pan; thick gravy
steps.cameraCheck: The keema with a spoonful lifted
steps.watchOut: Catching and sticking at the bottom means the heat is too high or water is gone; add 2 tbsp hot water and scrape.

steps.title: Dry it down
steps.text: Remove the lid and cook on medium heat, stirring, until thick.
steps.visualCue: A spoon leaves a trail; oil shimmers on top; no watery pool
steps.videoShot: A spoon dragged through the keema leaving a trail.
steps.watchOut: Still watery means keep going; if it starts to stick, switch off and let the heat finish it.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Switch off the heat, stir in ½ tsp (1 g) garam masala, half the coriander and 1 tsp lemon juice.
steps.tip: Spoon off any pool of oil on top for a lighter dish (not counted in section 5).
steps.visualCue: Fresh aroma, bright green flecks, glossy surface
steps.watchOut: Garam masala cooked for long goes bitter; add it only after the heat is off.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Cover for 2 minutes, then serve (about 170 g) with the remaining coriander and the lemon wedge.
steps.visualCue: Gravy settles and clings to the mince; steam rising
steps.videoShot: A slow pan over the plate.
steps.watchOut: Serving straight from the flame makes it look thin; the short rest thickens it.

reasons: complete protein (about 30 g) with iron, zinc and B12, no deep frying and no added sugar. Points off for saturated fat (about 8 g), about 1,120 mg sodium and cholesterol of about 110 mg. Restaurants usually use more oil or ghee, more salt and fattier mince, and often serve it with buttered bread.

researchRating.basis: mutton keema is a staple across India with many recipe versions (Archana's Kitchen, Indian Healthy Recipes, Sharmis Passions, Ranveer Brar, Slurrp, Sanjeev Kapoor) and Mumbai restaurant menus. Points off because review counts and comments were not visible (pages seen only through search snippets) and it is rich in fat and salt.

storage: Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 3 days (cool within 1 hour); freezes for up to 2 months. Reheat in a pan with 2 tbsp water on low until steaming hot all the way through, or microwave covered for 2 minutes, stirring once.
leftoverRemix: Keema paratha or keema toastie. Use cold keema as a paratha stuffing (mix with chopped coriander) or spread it between two slices of bread with cheese and grill until crisp. (Cheese or bread changes the diet tags.)
burnOff: about 6.2 km of running (435 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 8.7 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 45 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: mutton, onion and garlic are avoided

ekadashi.reason: meat, onion and garlic are avoided

jain.reason: meat, onion, garlic and fresh ginger

ramadan.reason: use halal-sourced mutton; keema with roti is a common sehri or iftar dish, but about 1,100 mg sodium (est.) can add to thirst during the fast, so cut the salt to 2 g

jain.reason: mutton, onion, garlic and fresh ginger; Jain rules exclude meat and root vegetables

vegan.reason: mutton (the recipe uses oil, no dairy)

sattvik.reason: contains onion and garlic, and meat

glutenFree.reason: no wheat, rava or hing in this recipe; serve with rice or a gluten-free bread (roti and pav are wheat); check the garam masala label

dairyFree.reason: cooked in sunflower oil, no butter, ghee, curd or cream
